subject: general
question: Which body is entrusted with recruiting India’s civil servants on the basis of merit?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Union Public Service Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)** is India's premier central recruiting agency responsible for conducting examinations to select civil servants based on merit.
 
• Established under **Article 315 of the Constitution of India**, the UPSC is an autonomous body that ensures impartial recruitment of candidates to the civil services.
 
• The UPSC conducts various exams such as the **Civil Services Examination (CSE)**, which selects candidates for prestigious services like the IAS, IPS, IFS, and others.
 
• The Commission functions independently and is protected under the Constitution to ensure that its operations remain unbiased and free from political influence.
 
• The headquarters of the UPSC is located at **Dholpur House, New Delhi**, and it plays a critical role in recruiting candidates for various posts under the Central Government.
 
• The recruitment process includes **preliminary exams, mains exams, and a personal interview** to ensure that the candidates meet the high standards required for civil services in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UPSC Constitutional Provisions:**

 
 
• The UPSC is governed by **Articles 315 to 323** of the Indian Constitution, which outline the structure, functions, and independence of the Commission.
 
• The Commission consists of a **Chairman and other members** appointed by the President of India.
 
• The term of office for UPSC members is **six years or until the age of 65 years**, whichever is earlier.
 
 
 
• **Functions of UPSC:**
 
 
• Conducting examinations for appointments to the civil services of the Union, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS), and Indian Foreign Service (IFS).
 
• Advising the President and Governors on matters related to recruitment, transfers, promotions, and disciplinary actions of civil servants.
 
• Ensuring fair and transparent recruitment processes for various Group A and Group B posts under the Central Government.
 
 
 
• **Historical Background:**
 
 
• The UPSC traces its origins to the **Public Service Commission established in 1926** under British rule.
 
• Post-independence, the Commission was reconstituted as the Union Public Service Commission in **1950**, following the adoption of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Examinations Conducted:**
 
 
• Some of the major exams conducted by UPSC include the **Civil Services Examination (CSE)**, **Indian Engineering Services (IES)**, **Indian Forest Services (IFoS)**, **Combined Defense Services (CDS)**, and more.
 
• The exams are highly competitive, with lakhs of candidates appearing every year for a limited number of posts.
 
 
 
• **Significance of UPSC:**
 
 
• UPSC ensures **merit-based selection**, promoting efficiency and integrity in the governance of the country.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in strengthening the administrative structure of India by recruiting highly qualified and competent individuals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **UPSC vs State Public Service Commissions:**

 
 
• While UPSC handles recruitment for central civil services, **State Public Service Commissions (SPSC)** conduct exams for state-level administrative posts.
 
• Both are independent constitutional bodies, but their jurisdiction differs based on the level of governance.
 
 
 
• **Autonomy and Accountability:**
 
 
• The independence of UPSC is safeguarded to ensure unbiased recruitment, but it remains accountable to the Parliament and the President of India.
 
• The Commission submits an **annual report** to the President, detailing its activities and recommendations.
 
 
 
• **UPSC Examination Process:**
 
 
• The Civil Services Examination consists of three stages: **Prelims, Mains, and Interview**.
 
• Preliminary exams test general knowledge and aptitude, while the mains focus on specialized subjects. The interview assesses personality and decision-making capabilities.
